html:
On 19 March 1946 a French law made French Guiana, Martinique, Guadeloupe and Réunion overseas departments, legally part of France itself rather than colonies.

The poet Aimé Césaire of Martinique pushed the law, hoping equal status would bring the same rights and welfare as in mainland France. French Guiana gained French social benefits, schools and pay scales, paid for by Paris, and a prefect replaced the governor.

Since then it has had a much higher income than its neighbours Suriname and Brazil, but also high prices and dependence on France. It is the largest part of the European Union outside Europe and uses the euro. Strikes in 2017 shut down the territory over crime and neglect. Its capital, Cayenne, is the seat of its government.
sum: On 19 March 1946 a French law made French Guiana, Martinique, Guadeloupe and Réunion overseas departments, legally part of France itself rather than colonies.
